heroLead: Bolivar sits along the Loyalhanna near the Westmoreland-Indiana County line, in a corner of the state that saw legacy shallow oil and gas wells long before Marcellus ever came up.
intro: This part of Westmoreland County has a longer oil and gas history than most people realize, with shallow conventional wells dotting family farms going back generations, well before the Marcellus Shale became a household term. If your family holds minerals near Bolivar, there's a decent chance the deed history includes an old conventional lease from decades ago, layered underneath whatever more recent Marcellus activity has come through since.

We know how confusing it is to sort out which lease covers which formation when a family's paperwork spans two very different eras of drilling. That's the kind of title work we do before ever quoting a number.

sections.heading: Two eras of drilling on the same land
paragraphs: Legacy shallow wells in this part of the state typically produced from formations well above the Marcellus interval, often under leases with very different, and sometimes much simpler, royalty terms than what's standard today. A modern Marcellus lease on the same tract is a separate agreement covering the deeper formation, and the two can coexist without conflicting, though it takes careful title review to confirm exactly what each one covers.

Wells in this area can produce from either the shallower conventional zones or the deeper Marcellus and Utica formations, so the value of your interest depends heavily on which formations are actually being produced.

sections.heading: Old wells, old paperwork
paragraphs: If your family's oldest lease predates modern recordkeeping standards, we work through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds to build a clean chain of title, connecting the original grant to your current ownership even across several generations of transfers.

sections.heading: What your interest is worth today
paragraphs: Once we've confirmed exactly what formations and units your interest participates in, we build an offer based on actual production history rather than a rough county-wide average.

faqs.question: My family has an old oil lease from the 1970s. Does that affect a Marcellus sale?
faqs.answer: It can. Older shallow-well leases typically cover different formations than a Marcellus lease on the same land. We review both to confirm exactly what you own and what's currently producing.

faqs.question: Are legacy shallow wells worth anything at all today?
faqs.answer: Some are still marginally producing and generate a small royalty; others have gone dry. We'll check actual production records for your specific well before evaluating.

faqs.question: Can I sell just my Marcellus-depth rights and keep the shallow rights?
faqs.answer: In some cases, yes, if your deeds clearly separate the formations. We'll tell you whether that's an option once we've reviewed your title.
